claim: FLARE's fine-grained bug-suspiciousness signal is produced by a separately trained bidirectional-transformer diagnostic model, not by the code-generating LLM's own self-reported confidence.
stance_target: FLARE occupies the proposed headline of a code LLM expressing its OWN calibrated confidence
quoted_support: We train a diagnostic model f_theta that outputs line-level suspiciousness scores... We train the full diagnostic model from scratch, including the input embeddings, transformer encoder, and linear prediction head.

claim: FLARE predicts suspiciousness at the LINE level, not per-test-case or per-requirement granularity.
stance_target: FLARE occupies per-test-case/per-requirement structured confidence granularity
quoted_support: we train a diagnostic model f_theta that outputs line-level suspiciousness scores: r = f_theta(C) in R^L

claim: FLARE reports no AUROC or calibration metric anywhere in the paper; evaluation is Top-k localization accuracy and downstream Pass@1 refinement gains.
quoted_support: Table 4 reports Top-1, Top-3, and Top-10 accuracy... Flare achieves the strongest localization performance across all settings.

claim: FLARE uses execution feedback (visible test pass/fail counts) only to select among top-k candidate refinements, not to evaluate or train calibration of the diagnostic signal.
stance_target: role of execution verifiability in FLARE vs proposed paper
quoted_support: Flare prefers the candidate that passes more tests or resolves more failures... During refinement, execution feedback and candidate selection use only visible/public tests.

claim: FLARE(k=1), using only diagnostic localization without candidate search, outperforms the strongest prior baseline NL-Debugging by 1.72 to 7.42 percentage points absolute Pass@1 in 9 of 10 LiveCodeBench settings.
stance_target: FLARE's empirical performance vs prior refinement baselines
quoted_support: Even without candidate search (k=1), Flare outperforms the strongest baseline with an absolute improvement from 1.72% to 7.42%.

claim: The diagnostic model's training objective is a position-level cross-entropy over lexical-unit logits pointing to the single ground-truth buggy unit, not a calibration-style proper scoring rule.
quoted_support: We train the model with position-level cross-entropy over lexical-unit logits: L_FL = -log( exp(s_j*) / sum_m exp(s_m) ).

claim: Removing fine-grained diagnostic feedback (execution-only ablation) drops Pass@1 by 4.59-4.70 points at k=1 and by 6.85-10.18 points at k=10 relative to full FLARE, showing localization signal has independent value beyond execution feedback.
stance_target: value of fine-grained localization signal independent of execution feedback
quoted_support: At k=1, execution-only refinement reaches 50.27% Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench and 53.81% on BigCodeBench, while full Flare reaches 54.86% and 58.51%.

claim: FLARE's failure-case analysis attributes 60.53% of remaining failures to language-model reasoning failure (localization correct but model cannot fix the bug), suggesting line-localization alone is insufficient for a large share of hard cases.
stance_target: limits of line-level localization for code repair
scope_conditions: 418 manually inspected failure cases from BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench
quoted_support: Language Model Reasoning Failure (60.53%). Most failures reflect cases where localization identifies useful regions, but the language model still lacks the capability to perform the required reasoning or algorithmic change.
